study.title: Radiation reduction for interventional radiology imaging: a video frame interpolation solution

imaging.modality_detail: IR sequences in three modes: unsubtracted angiography, subtraction (DSA), and fluoroscopy
imaging.territory_detail: Pediatric abdominal/peripheral interventions; arterial, venous and portal vein angiography across various regions (e.g., splenic, hepatic)

data_released.detail: Image data not shareable under agreement with data custodian; model and de-identified reader outputs available on request

task.task_description: Video frame interpolation of simulated low-frame-rate IR sequences (every other frame removed) to restore high-frame-rate sequences, enabling reduced acquisition frame rate.
task.clinical_application: Radiation dose reduction in pediatric interventional radiology

temporal_evidence.quote: These kernels were applied in the convolution process of preceding and succeeding frames, and their output features were fused to generate the interpolated intermediate frame.

metrics.metric: Radiologist votes Ground Truth / Uncertain / SepConv++

model_weights_available.detail: Model available upon request to the corresponding authors

G1.quote: our IR sequences were obtained from pediatric patients undergoing peripheral interventions at a single imaging center

G2.quote: The applicability of our deep learning model requires further verification on sequences obtained from diverse imaging devices.

G3.quote: our study is the first to explore this application on IR images with noticeable motions

G6.quote: Our future work will involve evaluating the model's performance through clinical animal trials to quantify radiation dose reduction

other_limitations: Pediatric-only cohort; transferability to adults with different blood flow untested
Sequences with significant motion (e.g., cardiac interventions) not included
Radiation dose reduction simulated retrospectively, not measured
future_work: Verify model on sequences from diverse imaging devices and institutions
Investigate transfer from pediatric to adult populations
Experiments on sequences with significant motion such as cardiac interventions
Clinical animal trials to quantify radiation dose reduction
Develop a model applicable across modalities, demographics and lesion locations
